records.summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. Provincially, the only incident-level signal is a police-intervention pattern: forces of this, Salta and Buenos Aires provinces intervened in the deaths of three LGBT+ people over eight days (18-26 November 2025), with one national report that treats a single provincial case as meaningful in a low-count country.

records.name: La Roja
records.summary: No trans-related provincial statute, enforcement series or incident pattern specific to La Rioja was documented in the country dossier — but "no signal" there means "no documentation", not "no exposure": like every Argentine province it retains contravención/faltas police codes identified by an NGO survey as the instrument behind most arrests of trans and travesti people, and, like other interior provinces, it has neither a visible community presence nor reporting infrastructure to generate records. The February 2025 national decrees curtailing the Gender Identity Law — banning gender-transition hormone and surgical treatment for minors and changing prison placement of trans people — apply here as in all provinces, against a deteriorating national picture (a record 227 anti-LGBT hate crimes in 2025, up 62% year-on-year).

records.name: Mendoza
records.summary:
No Mendoza-specific statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is documented for transgender visitors. That silence is not reassuring: interior provinces without local reporting infrastructure generate few records even where risk is real, and the country-wide security picture for trans and travesti people has sharply deteriorated.

What is documented is national. Per a March 2026 report by the LGBT news agency Agencia Presentes, drawing on the national hate-crime observatory's tally, at least 227 attacks motivated by sexual orientation or gender identity were recorded in 2025 — up 62% year-on-year, the highest figure of the observatory's decade of operation, roughly one every 38 hours — with perpetrators predominantly security-force personnel and unidentified attackers in public space, beatings the main modality, and the observatory attributing the surge to the national government's 'cultural battle' against LGBTI+ people. Attacks continued into early 2026, including a life-endangering home invasion of the president of an LGBTIQ+ organisation in a northern province. An April 2025 Blade feature described the transgender community as facing a 'chaotic, desperate situation' amid government policies; the underlying page is no longer retrievable.
